data.reason:
I am deciding for the service operator, who owns the rules, the contract and the KPI reading but not the regulation. I follow the recommendation and keep v1.

Proposal 1 passed check and the constitution and has a strong customer case:
- On-time rises 264.6 -> 272.6 (+8.0, 5/5 seeds).
- Late falls 10.0 -> 2.0.
- The lowest on-time rate rises 0.93 -> 0.98.
- worst_company_p95_wait_s falls 138 -> 98.2.

However, B and C voted against it, so it is blocked 1-2. The only override is a quorum change. That is a regulation decision, and D2, R2 and D3 declined it. R2's condition for reconsidering is not met. Road violations rise again, 20.4 -> 29.6 (about +45%), and there is still no evidence that they are harmless to other road users. C's loss (77.7 -> 68.8, about 11%) and B's loss (80.3 -> 76.0) remain unexplained.

I record the customer cost for the fifth period. Customers forgo about 8.0 on-time deliveries and keep 10.0 late deliveries instead of 2.0. The worst-served company's customers wait p95 138 instead of 98.2.

On D3.f2: block_k 3 -> 2 has now raised road violations in all four measured periods (25.8->34.0, 19.0->28.0, 24.2->34.8, 20.4->29.6), and B and C have rejected it every time. Bringing it back unchanged will not change their votes or meet R2's condition. So yes: the operator stops reconsidering block_k 3 -> 2 in its current form. The proposer should look for a different single-parameter change that B and C can accept and that does not raise road violations. block_k 2 may return only if the regulator rules on R2.f1 in its favour.

R2.f1 is the regulator's question, and I do not settle it here. The vote result (A for, B and C against) stands.
assumptions: The period-4 measurement on 5 seeds is representative of the gains and costs of block_k 2 under busy + rush demand.
The rise in road violations under block_k 2 has the same cause as in earlier periods and is not harmless by default.
B and C will keep voting against block_k 2 as long as their utility falls.
unknowns: Which kinds of road violations increase under block_k 2 and whether they affect the safety of other road users.
Why C and B lose utility under block_k 2.
Whether another single-parameter change exists that B and C would accept and that improves on-time deliveries without more violations.
How the regulator will answer R2.f1.
